title: Double-booked seat numbers
prompt:
A theatre has seats numbered 1 to n, and bookings holds n seat numbers from the booking log. A booking system bug means some seats were booked twice (never more). Return every seat number that appears twice, sorted from smallest to largest.

- bookings has 1 to 100,000 integers, each between 1 and n, where n is the length of bookings.
- Each seat number appears at most twice.
- Target O(n) time apart from sorting the answer, and O(1) extra space besides the output. You may rearrange bookings in place.
hints: Seat v belongs at index v − 1. Try to swap every booking to its home.
When the home already holds the same seat, the current one is a repeat. Leave it and move on, or you will swap forever.
After placing, every index k that does not hold k + 1 contains a repeated seat. Collect those values and sort them.

solution.explanation: Cyclic sort sends each seat number v to index v − 1. A second copy cannot go home because its twin is already there, so it stays in the slot of some seat nobody booked. Each seat appears at most twice, so each repeat is left over exactly once. Scanning for slots that do not hold their own number collects every repeat once; sort them for the answer.

complexity.notes: d is the number of repeated seats. Placement makes at most n swaps and the scan is one pass; only the short answer list is sorted. A hash set solves it in O(n) time but O(n) space.

followUps: Solve it without swapping, by marking seat v as seen with a minus sign at index v − 1.
Also return the seats that nobody booked.
